features.name: 3D surface expressions
steps: Open Desmos 3D
Enter z=xy in the expression field
Parse the 3D variable relationships of x, y, and z
The corresponding surface is generated in the 3D coordinate system
Change it to z=sin(xy)
The old surface is replaced in real time by the new oscillating surface
Keep the current camera view and coordinate range
features.expected: A 3D expression must be parsed correctly and generate the corresponding surface; after modifying the expression the old surface is replaced in real time; the current camera view and coordinate range are preserved.

features.name: Combined display of multiple surfaces
steps: Enter z=xy
Add a second expression z=sin(xy)
Both surfaces are displayed in the same 3D coordinate system
Toggle the visibility state on the left of each expression separately
Hide one of the surfaces individually
Then restore the display
The two expressions keep their colors, order, and content
features.expected: Both surfaces must be displayed at the same time; after toggling visibility, hiding/restoring each one individually works correctly; colors, order, and content are preserved.

features.name: 3D camera rotation / zoom / pan
steps: Create a surface with an obviously three-dimensional structure
Rotate the 3D view by dragging with the mouse
Change the distance with the scroll wheel or the zoom buttons
Switch to a preset viewing direction
Then restore the default orientation
The surface data itself does not change; only the view matrix changes
features.expected: Rotation / zoom / pan only change the view matrix while the surface data is unchanged; after restoring the default orientation the view is correct.

features.name: Default orientation / XY view
steps: Enter z=xy
Tap the preset-direction button in the top-right corner
Switch from the default perspective to the XY viewing direction
The 3D surface is displayed close to a flat projection
Then switch back to the default orientation
Keep the expressions and coordinate range unchanged
features.expected: After switching to the XY view the surface is displayed close to a flat projection; after switching back to the default view the expressions and coordinate range are unchanged.

features.name: 3D coordinate-range settings
steps: Create a surface
Open the graph settings
Modify the minimum and maximum of the x-axis, y-axis, and z-axis separately
The 3D bounding box and surface clipping range update in sync
Close the settings panel
The values are preserved after reopening
features.expected: After modifying the coordinate range the bounding box and the surface clipping range update in sync; the values are preserved after closing and reopening the settings panel.

features.name: Axis / grid display control
steps: Open the graph settings
Turn off the "2D plane" or grid-type display
Toggle "show numbers" and "3D axis labels"
Observe the coordinate plane, tick numbers, and x/y/z labels changing immediately
Then restore the default combination
The mathematical surface stays unchanged
features.expected: Toggling the coordinate plane / tick numbers / axis labels takes effect immediately; after restoring the default combination the mathematical surface stays unchanged.

features.name: Rendering property combinations
steps: Create a 3D surface
Open the graph settings
Toggle display options such as lighting, inverted colors, and semi-transparent surfaces in turn
Each modification only affects the visual rendering of the surface
Adjust the viewing angle to confirm that transparency and lighting effects change correctly with the view
The expression data stays unchanged
features.expected: Toggling lighting/inverted colors/semi-transparency only affects rendering; transparency and lighting change correctly with the view; the expression data does not change.

features.name: Disable zoom / disable rotation
steps: Create a surface and adjust the current view
Enable "disable zoom" and "disable rotation" in the graph settings
Try scroll-wheel zooming and mouse rotation
The corresponding interaction is blocked
Disable the lock again
Normal 3D interaction is restored
features.expected: After enabling zoom/rotation lock the corresponding interactions are blocked; after disabling the lock normal 3D interaction is restored.

features.name: Auxiliary math keyboard
steps: Open the auxiliary keyboard in the bottom-left corner
Use the built-in x / y / z / aᵇ / π / √ / parentheses / operators buttons to enter the 3D expression
Form a valid expression such as z=x²+y²
3D surface generation
Collapse the auxiliary keyboard
The expressions and surfaces are preserved
features.expected: An expression entered with the auxiliary keyboard must be parsed correctly and generate the surface; after collapsing the keyboard the expression and surface are preserved.

features.name: Building composite functions with the auxiliary keyboard
steps: Create an expression
Use the auxiliary math keyboard and the "Functions" panel to enter z=sin(xy), exponential, or radical expressions
Each completed syntax structure is parsed in real time
Modify an internal parameter
Continuous updates of a 3D surface
Existing other expressions are not affected
features.expected: A composite function entered via the auxiliary keyboard is parsed in real time; changing parameters updates it continuously; other expressions are unaffected.

features.name: Add expressions / notes / tables / regressions / folders
steps: Tap the "+" in the top-left corner
Confirm in turn that expressions, notes, tables, regressions, and folders can be added
Create notes and tables
Add another mathematical expression
Entries of different types are kept in order in the left-hand list
Deleting one of the items does not affect the others
features.expected: Added expressions / notes / tables / regressions / folders must be saved in order; deleting one item does not affect the others.

features.name: Expression duplication and batch editing
steps: Create z=xy
Enter expression management mode
Duplicate the expression
Change the copy to z=3xy or another variant
Both objects are displayed at the same time
Delete one of them
Exit management mode
The remaining expressions and surfaces continue to exist
features.expected: The copied expression must be independently editable; both objects are displayed at once; after deleting one the others continue to exist.

features.name: Tables driving 3D data
steps: Add a table
Enter several groups of x, y, z or related data columns
Use this data to generate a visualization object or as a variable in later expressions
Modify one row of data
The related points or objects in the graph update in sync
After deleting the data the graph changes in sync
features.expected: The table data must drive the visualization objects; after modifying a row the related objects update in sync; after deleting data they change in sync.

features.name: Parametric 3D objects
steps: Define a parameter or slider, e.g. a=1
Create a 3D expression that depends on a parameter
Change a
The surface shape, scale, or position changes in real time
Then add a second parameter
Multiple parameters jointly control the same 3D object
features.expected: Parameters / sliders must drive 3D objects in real time; multiple parameters jointly control the same object.

features.name: Linked 3D expressions
steps: First define a=2 and f(x,y)=a·sin(xy)
Then enter z=f(x,y)
Modify a
The existing 3D surface is recomputed automatically
Deleting the function definition puts the dependent expression into an invalid state
When the definition is restored the surface reappears
features.expected: After changing the parameter the dependent surface is recomputed automatically; deleting the function definition puts the dependent expression into an invalid state; when the definition is restored the surface reappears.

features.name: Angle-mode switching
steps: Create a 3D surface containing trigonometric functions
Open settings
Switch between radian and degree modes
The same expression is recomputed under the new angle interpretation
The surface changes accordingly
Switching back to the original mode restores the original result
features.expected: After switching between radian/degree mode the same expression is recomputed under the new interpretation; switching back restores the original result.

features.name: Expression error recovery
steps: Enter a valid 3D expression
Change it to an expression with incomplete syntax or wrong variable relationships
The system stops generating the object or shows an error state
Fix the expression
The surface is restored automatically without recreating the entry
features.expected: On a syntax error the system stops generating or shows an error state; after fixing it the surface is restored automatically without recreating the entry.

features.name: State preservation in complex multi-object scenarios
steps: Create two 3D surfaces, a table, a note, and several parameters
Adjust the coordinate range, hide one of the surfaces, and rotate the view
Edit another expression
Then restore the hidden object
The order, visibility, parameter values, coordinate settings, and current camera state of all objects stay consistent
features.expected: In multi-object scenarios the order / visibility / parameter values / coordinate settings and camera state must stay consistent.

features.name: Save and reopen a graph
steps: Build several expressions and a custom 3D view
Save a graph
Leave the current page
Reopen the graph from Saved Work
The expressions, order, surfaces, coordinate ranges, and persistable settings are restored
Continue modifying and save again
features.expected: After saving and reopening, the expressions/order/surfaces/coordinate ranges and persistable settings must be restored; after further modification it can be saved again.

exclusions.feature:
Multi-user real-time collaboration / shared editing
Exclude simultaneous editing by several users, remote cursors, real-time sync, and conflict handling
exclusions.reason: Depends on accounts, multi-user sessions, and WebSocket/real-time sync services and is not part of the core 3D math graphing capability

exclusions.feature:
External sharing chains
Exclude social sharing, the public-link permission system, and email sharing
exclusions.reason: It mainly depends on external identity and sharing infrastructure and cannot effectively measure a 3D-graphing agent

exclusions.feature:
Full account system
Exclude registration, login, avatars, account security, and account recovery
exclusions.reason: The identity system is not part of Desmos 3D's core computation and graphing capabilities

exclusions.feature:
Exact reproduction of the Desmos cloud-save infrastructure
A local or simulated implementation of "state restored after save/reopen" is kept; reproducing the real Desmos cloud database is not required
exclusions.reason: The benchmark should test state persistence rather than the Desmos backend account architecture; retained surface: f01 3D surface expressions, f19 save and reopen a graph

exclusions.feature:
Full version-history implementation
Full historical version browsing, cloud restore strategies, and cross-device version sync can be excluded
exclusions.reason: It requires complex persistence infrastructure and contributes little to the core 3D graphing capability

exclusions.feature:
Physical keyboard / IME cross-platform compatibility matrix
Covering all Windows, macOS, Linux, and mobile IME differences is not required
exclusions.reason: It is costly to reproduce and weakly related to the core mathematical features; the in-page auxiliary math keyboard cannot be excluded

exclusions.feature:
Screen readers / Braille / audio graphs
Exclude advanced accessibility audio feedback, Braille devices, and dedicated assistive hardware
exclusions.reason: It requires extra platform capabilities; however, ordinary keyboard operation and the in-page math keyboard should still be kept; retained surface: f09 auxiliary math keyboard

exclusions.feature:
All extreme boundaries of the math engine
Fully reproducing Desmos' internal algorithms for all special functions, singularities, extremely large values, floating-point boundaries, and numerical stability is not required
exclusions.reason: It should reproduce mainstream functions and core expression semantics but must not turn the benchmark into a full CAS/numerical-analysis engine rewrite

exclusions.feature:
The complete set of advanced statistics/probability functions
Moving all statistics distributions and inference functions from the Calculator into the 3D benchmark is not required
exclusions.reason: The core of the 3D product is 3D functions and spatial interaction; only the parts that support representative data tasks should be kept

exclusions.feature:
Exact GPU rendering consistency
Materials, anti-aliasing, lighting, and transparency ordering are not required to match the official app pixel by pixel
exclusions.reason: The visuals should correctly express 3D relationships, but pixel-level WebGL consistency should not be the criterion for functional success

exclusions.feature:
The full mobile gesture and responsive set
Exclude all phone/tablet-specific layouts, two-finger rotation, and mobile soft keyboards
exclusions.reason: The current benchmark can be limited to a desktop web environment to avoid device differences polluting the results

exclusions.feature:
Full internationalization
Full support for all languages, RTL, and regional number formats is not required
exclusions.reason: A single language environment can be fixed; internationalization is not part of the core 3D graphing chain

exclusions.feature:
Help center / tutorials / external documents
Exclude help pages, product tutorials, and external linked documents
exclusions.reason: It belongs to a content-support system and does not reflect 3D graphing itself

exclusions.feature:
Exact brand visual assets
Fully reproducing the Desmos logo, official icon assets, and non-functional visual details is not required
exclusions.reason: The benchmark should focus on structure and interaction and must not be constrained by branded copyrighted assets

exclusions.feature:
Backend telemetry / analytics / recommendation system
Exclude analytics tracking, A/B tests, and personalized recommendations
exclusions.reason: It is not directly observable by the user and is unrelated to mathematical graphing
